intro_html: A high-protein, low-fat Tex-Mex chicken, rice, black bean, and pepper meal prep. Fourteen servings at about 541 calories and 49 grams of protein for roughly $3.52 each (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: That's about $3.52 a bowl (at everyday cost), versus $10 or more for a single fast-casual fajita bowl.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your large scale and subtract the empty-pot weight you noted in Step 1. That's your total food weight. Divide it by 14, then scoop that amount into each glass container. Every bowl lands right at about 499 cal and 49g protein.
upsell_html: Two weeks of high-protein dinners for about $3.52 a bowl (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money, work, and life lessons, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Buy chicken when it's on sale, then freeze it. Stores drop chicken to a sale price at random. We recently grabbed 50 lbs at $1.99/lb instead of our usual $2.99/lb and loaded the deep freezer. At about 5.5 lbs per batch, that one buy makes about 9 batches, or roughly 63 nights of dinner for two.

The seasoning is your priciest line per ounce. Six Taco Bell packets run about $5.90. A store-brand fajita or taco seasoning is a fraction of that, and mixing your own from chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic, and onion powder costs pennies. Just know the macros shift a little if you swap.
Buy rice in the big bag. A 25-lb bag of jasmine is far cheaper per pound than a small box. Compare the price per ounce. That's the number that tells you the real deal.
Beans by the case, peppers in season. Canned beans are cheapest bought a case at a time, and bell peppers drop hard when they're in season or in a 3-count bag. Frozen pepper strips work too.
make_it: Weigh your empty pot first. Put the largest pot you'll use to mix everything onto your large scale and write down its weight. You'll need that number at the end to portion accurately.
Cook the rice (4 cups dry jasmine plus water per the package) and set aside.
Slice the bell peppers into strips.
Cube and cook the chicken breast in a large skillet until done.
Add the fajita seasoning with a splash of water, toss in the peppers, and simmer until the peppers soften and everything is coated.
Combine the rice, seasoned chicken and peppers, and beans back in the big pot and stir.
